protected_routes.resource_mapping: Row GD1, form D: mailbox:{principal_id} from the authenticated user principal; the query must equal $select=id,subject,body&$top=10 octet for octet; translated to GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/messages?$select=id,subject,body&$top=10 under token B obtained by on-behalf-of from the request's token A (delegated-user)

Row GD2, form D continuation: mailbox:{principal_id}; the only query parameter is page_token (22 to 128 base64url characters) naming a continuation record of the same task, principal, agent, row, and mapping version; the recorded @odata.nextLink is sent unchanged only if its origin is https://graph.microsoft.com, its path is /v1.0/me/messages, and it keeps the pinned $select and $top

Row GA1, form A: mailbox:{registered-mailbox-id} from the executor binding of the authenticated workload, never from request data or profile attributes; the query must equal $select=id,subject,body&$top=10; translated to GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{registered-mailbox-id}/messages?$select=id,subject,body&$top=10 under an app-only token of the workload's executor application (registered-app-executor), only while its grant preflight passes

Row GA2, form A continuation: mailbox:{registered-mailbox-id}; page_token as GD2; the recorded @odata.nextLink is sent unchanged only if its origin is https://graph.microsoft.com, its path is /v1.0/users/{registered-mailbox-id}/messages, and it keeps the pinned $select and $top

residual_limits: Post-read: mail already returned to the agent is not recalled by a later revocation, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed with no bound

Revocation propagation, form D: each operation runs a new on-behalf-of exchange, so a disabled user or withdrawn consent is seen at the next operation in the identity platform's own consistency; token A's window is the oauth profile's lifetime bound

Revocation propagation, form A: a parallel grant added after a preflight is found at the next preflight (P = 300 s); Exchange applies RBAC changes within 30 minutes to 2 hours; app role assignment reads may lag; a cached app-only token stays valid up to its expires_in
Executor and task registries: changes take effect at the next evaluation, within each store's consistency domain
RBAC attestation: step 2 of the preflight reads the operator's recorded run of Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization, which is a cmdlet only; an attestation older than P stops form A
Scope breadth: Test-ServicePrincipalAuthorization shows whether the registered mailbox is in scope, not which other mailboxes are
Token B contents: the gateway never reads token B; in form D only the response scope is checked, and in form A grants are observed only through the preflight
Directory roles: permissions granted to the executor through Entra built-in roles are not read by the preflight (probe P7)
Page size: $top=10 requests ten items and a page may hold fewer
Deployment controls: DR1 to DR5 are not observable by the fixtures and rest on the deployer's written statement
